registry_purpose: A date-bounded, evidence-linked decision register for frontier technology adoption in KJDS.

decision_vocabulary.adopt_now: Approved to enter a scoped implementation slice; not proof that implementation or production rollout is complete.
decision_vocabulary.pilot: Approved only for an isolated, reversible experiment with measured acceptance criteria.
decision_vocabulary.watch: Monitor upstream maturity and KJDS demand; do not add a runtime dependency.
decision_vocabulary.reject_now: Do not adopt under current architecture and scale; reconsider only when the stated entry gate is met.

gate_semantics.entry_gate: Conditions and authorization required to start the decision-specific activity.
gate_semantics.exit_gate: Evidence required before production dependency or broader rollout can be considered.

current_kjds_baseline.agent_runtime: In-process governed routing, redaction, GenAI-style spans and deterministic eval records are implemented; a durable provider-neutral run/eval Evidence ledger is not implemented.
current_kjds_baseline.workflow: KJDS state machines and transactional outbox remain canonical; no Temporal runtime is installed.
current_kjds_baseline.retrieval: Evidence, PostgreSQL and the canonical Graph are available; no production GraphRAG or vector store is installed.
current_kjds_baseline.database: PostgreSQL 17 is the declared runtime baseline and PostgreSQL 18 is rehearsal-only; the running patch level was not observable during the 2026-08-03 review, and PostgreSQL 17.10 or later is required before fresh deployment evidence can pass.
current_kjds_baseline.web: Next.js 16.2.11 and React 19.2.7 are installed; individual frontier rendering and caching patterns still require measured, scope-safe acceptance.
current_kjds_baseline.analytics: PostgreSQL remains the only operating truth store; ClickHouse and Iceberg are not runtime dependencies.

coverage_scope.included: Frontier dependencies or bounded implementation candidates selected for a KJDS adoption, pilot, watch, or reject decision.
existing_baselines_not_separate_candidat: current Next.js and React runtime versions
existing KJDS state machines, outbox, Evidence, Graph, and governed Agent runtime

adopt_now.decision_rationale: KJDS already has in-process governed runs, GenAI-style spans and deterministic eval records; persisting provider-neutral run, model, prompt-template, tool, Evidence, authority and outcome lineage closes the remaining auditability gap without creating a second control plane.

maturity.evidence_basis: Official Responses API, Agents SDK tracing, graders, and eval APIs are published.

kjds_use_cases: Bind model, prompt, tool, Evidence, scope authority, latency, cost, and outcome to one agent run.
Regression-test extraction, research, profit-readiness, and operating-gate agents before promotion.
risks: Trace payloads may expose prompts, tool arguments, credentials, or tenant data.
Provider-specific trace schemas can leak into canonical business contracts.
Weak graders can reward fluent but unsupported conclusions.

criteria: Define a provider-neutral AgentRun envelope and redaction policy.
Choose at least one read-only workflow with a frozen eval corpus.
Keep Evidence and scope authority as canonical KJDS references.
Zero secret or cross-tenant leakage in trace fixtures.
Deterministic replay records model, prompt, tool, Evidence, and authority versions.
Eval thresholds and human escalation are enforced in CI without granting external write.

adopt_now.decision_rationale: G1 already verifies code, migrations, tests, builds, and images; signed provenance plus software and AI/ML BOMs can make that evidence portable and independently verifiable.

maturity.evidence_basis: SLSA 1.2 and the CycloneDX AI/ML BOM guidance are published standards and guidance.

kjds_use_cases: Bind G1 commit, migration head, image digests, dependencies, models, datasets, and prompts to attestations.
Verify deployable artifacts before commercial-pilot or hosted promotion.
Bind the resolved PostgreSQL image digest and patch version to deployment evidence instead of relying on a floating major-version tag.
risks: Unsigned or unverifiable attestations create compliance theater.
BOMs can leak private package names, model identifiers, or deployment topology.
Build provenance does not prove business correctness or Evidence quality.

criteria: Define the G1 subject digest and signer identity contract.
Classify public versus restricted BOM fields.
Use one existing API or Web image as the first subject.
Fresh-build verification fails closed on subject or signer drift.
SBOM and AI/ML BOM schemas validate and contain no secrets.
The resolved PostgreSQL image reports version 17.10 or later and its digest is present in the verified subject set.
Deployment policy checks provenance while remaining separate from business truth gates.

adopt_now.decision_rationale: Stable framework capabilities can simplify long-running operator views and build performance, but KJDS should adopt only measured patterns that preserve its existing design system and server authority boundaries.

maturity.evidence_basis: React 19.2 and Next.js 16 are officially released with documented APIs and migration guidance.

kjds_use_cases: Use Activity for preserving state in hidden operator workspaces where measured UX benefits exist.
Evaluate Cache Components, partial prerendering, React Compiler, and DevTools MCP without moving business decisions client-side.
risks: Cache boundaries can serve stale tenant- or scope-sensitive data.
Compiler or rendering changes can hide hydration and authorization regressions.
Framework novelty can displace higher-value business work.

criteria: Select one measured performance or state-preservation problem.
Document server-only authority and cache partitioning requirements.
Keep the existing visual language and accessibility baseline.
Full Web tests and production build pass.
Cross-tenant, auth, cache, and hydration negative tests pass.
Measured user or build benefit exceeds the maintenance cost.

pilot.decision_rationale: Durable execution may help multi-hour listing, recon, procurement, and recovery flows, but KJDS must first prove a gap in its persisted state machines and outbox rather than install a second workflow owner.

maturity.evidence_basis: Temporal documents durable execution, replay, task queues, and isolating nondeterministic I/O in Activities.

kjds_use_cases: Replay and recover a long-running read-only market-recon workflow.
Compare durable timers and human pauses with the existing KJDS state-machine and outbox contract.
risks: A second workflow control plane can split ownership and incident recovery.
Nondeterministic agent or network calls can break replay if placed in workflow code.
Operational overhead may exceed current workload needs.

criteria: Measure a real workflow that exceeds the current recovery or timer SLO.
Define one adapter boundary with KJDS remaining the business-state owner.
Use a read-only disposable environment.
Crash, retry, timeout, cancellation, and human-resume tests pass without duplicate effects.
Measured reliability benefit exceeds platform and on-call cost.
No second canonical business state or external-write bypass exists.

pilot.decision_rationale: KJDS has canonical graph and Evidence primitives that can support causal and temporal retrieval; a scoped pilot is preferable to a generic vector-chat memory layer.

maturity.evidence_basis: GraphRAG is an active open-source research project, while 2026 agent-memory evaluations show causal and tool-based retrieval advantages in specific tasks.

kjds_use_cases: Retrieve evidence-backed causal chains for SKU, variant, cost, campaign, and profit decisions.
Answer cross-case questions while preserving tenant, entity, store, time, and authority scope.
risks: Graph extraction can invent edges or collapse observation into fact.
Global community summaries can leak cross-tenant information.
Indexing and retrieval cost can exceed value on small datasets.

criteria: Freeze a read-only exact-scope question set with expected Evidence citations.
Use canonical KJDS nodes and edges; generated edges remain observations.
Define vector-only and deterministic graph baselines.
Citation precision, scope isolation, temporal validity, latency, and cost beat the baselines.
Unsupported edge and cross-scope leakage rates are zero in the acceptance corpus.
Memory cannot promote Fact, FinanceEntry, Pilot, Permit, or external write.

pilot.decision_rationale: The stable MCP 2026-07-28 authorization contract strengthens issuer, resource, audience, discovery, registration, and step-up behavior, but it must be mapped to KJDS Principal, exact scope, Evidence authority, and incremental permissions before use.

maturity.evidence_basis: The MCP 2026-07-28 specification is released and defines issuer validation, protected-resource metadata, resource indicators, audience binding, discovery, registration, refresh-token, and step-up rules; KJDS has not validated its Python SDK path against that revision.

kjds_use_cases: Issue audience-bound, least-privilege tokens to read-only research and Evidence tools.
Map incremental MCP scopes to KJDS exact-scope authority without accepting client-supplied tenant or entity identity.
risks: Token passthrough or confused-deputy behavior can cross trust boundaries.
Protocol scopes can be mistaken for KJDS business authority.
Remote server metadata and redirect validation create SSRF and phishing surfaces.
The 2026-07-28 stateless request and capability model is a breaking change from the currently installed Python SDK contract.

criteria: Choose one first-party read-only MCP server.
Freeze one supported protocol and SDK version before implementing issuer, audience, resource, redirect, registration, and incremental-scope validation.
Derive KJDS tenant and entity authority server-side.
Wrong issuer, audience, resource, scope, tenant, entity, store, or authority hash fails closed.
No token passthrough, bearer-token logging, or dynamic-client-registration abuse remains.
Revocation, expiry, rotation, audit, and incident tests pass.

pilot.decision_rationale: Portable agent telemetry is valuable, but GenAI semantic conventions now evolve in a separate repository and sensitive payload attributes require explicit opt-in, version pinning, and redaction.

maturity.evidence_basis: OpenTelemetry semantic conventions 1.43 mark GenAI conventions as moved to a separate repository; the old registry pages are deprecated, so KJDS requires a pinned translation boundary rather than domain-schema coupling.

kjds_use_cases: Export provider-neutral latency, token, cache, tool, and workflow metrics from the AgentRun contract.
Correlate agent spans with Evidence, authority, outbox, and operating-gate events using non-sensitive identifiers.
risks: Development attributes may change and break dashboards.
Prompt, tool-argument, and tool-result capture can expose personal, tenant, or secret data.
High-cardinality labels can create cost and availability problems.

criteria: Version-pin a translation layer instead of exposing semantic conventions to domain models.
Default all content-bearing attributes to disabled.
Set cardinality, retention, residency, and sampling budgets.
Schema-upgrade, redaction, tenant-isolation, cardinality, and sampling tests pass.
Zero prompt, tool payload, credential, or raw Evidence leakage in exported telemetry.
Dashboards improve incident or cost diagnosis against a no-OTel baseline.

pilot.decision_rationale: PostgreSQL 18 offers useful AIO, skip-scan, UUIDv7, OAuth, and temporal constraints, but KJDS should rehearse migrations and measure workloads before changing its PostgreSQL 17 baseline; security patching of PostgreSQL 17 remains an immediate baseline obligation, not a reason to skip the major-version pilot.

maturity.evidence_basis: PostgreSQL 18 is officially released with documented compatibility and feature changes; the 2026-05-14 security release establishes 18.4 and 17.10 as the reviewed secure patch lines.

kjds_use_cases: Benchmark Evidence, graph, profit, outbox, and scoped logistics query plans.
Evaluate UUIDv7, temporal WITHOUT OVERLAPS and PERIOD constraints, and OAuth in disposable environments.
risks: Extension, driver, collation, query-plan, or migration behavior may regress.
New temporal features can be mistaken for complete business-validity semantics.
An upgrade without rollback rehearsal can extend commercial downtime.
Conflating a required PostgreSQL 17 security patch with the PostgreSQL 18 pilot can either delay remediation or bypass major-version evidence.

criteria: Verify the PostgreSQL 17 baseline is patched to 17.10 or later independently of this pilot.
Freeze PostgreSQL 17 data, query, migration, extension, backup, and restore baselines.
Use a disposable PostgreSQL 18 database with production-like schema volume.
Define rollback and dual-version compatibility tests.
Migration replay, backup and restore, extension, driver, and rollback tests pass.
No critical query regresses beyond the agreed latency or lock budget.
A production migration runbook and independent recovery proof are approved.

pilot.decision_rationale: Signed policy bundles and privacy-safe decision logs may help infrastructure authorization, but OPA must not own KJDS business state, Evidence authority, Approval, or Permit decisions.

maturity.evidence_basis: OPA officially documents policy bundles and decision logs.

kjds_use_cases: Evaluate one deny-by-default, read-only infrastructure policy outside the business state machine.
Measure bundle rollback and privacy-safe decision-log value.
risks: Policy can diverge from canonical business authority.
Stale bundles can deny healthy work or allow obsolete policy.
Decision logs may contain sensitive inputs.

criteria: Select one read-only infrastructure decision with no money or external write.
Keep exact scope, Evidence, Approval, and Permit in KJDS.
Define signed bundle, rollback, redaction, and stale-policy behavior.
Bundle drift, stale state, outage, rollback, and privacy tests pass.
OPA and KJDS decisions cannot conflict silently.
Measured control or operations value exceeds the added platform cost.

watch.decision_rationale: Attested workload identity may strengthen a future hosted multi-service topology, but current KJDS deployment has not demonstrated a problem that justifies SPIRE operations and federation.

maturity.evidence_basis: SPIFFE/SPIRE specifications document workload attestation, SVIDs, and federation.

kjds_use_cases: Potentially attest API, worker, scheduler, and hosted-tool workloads without long-lived shared secrets.
Potentially federate workload identity across approved hosting boundaries.
risks: Workload identity can be confused with tenant, entity, store, user, or commercial authority.
Control-plane outage, rotation, or federation failure can block service.
Operations cost can exceed current secret-risk reduction.

criteria: A hosted multi-service identity problem is measured and not solved by current managed leases.
At least two non-production workloads require short-lived attested identity.
Workload identity is explicitly separated from KJDS exact-scope authority.
Attestation, rotation, federation, outage, rollback, and incident tests pass.
No workload SVID grants user, business, Approval, Permit, or external-write authority.
Measured risk reduction exceeds platform and on-call cost.

watch.decision_rationale: MCP Tasks has moved from the experimental 2025-11-25 core into an opt-in extension of the stable 2026-07-28 protocol, but the extension specification remains draft and SDK/provider support is uneven.

maturity.evidence_basis: The stable MCP 2026-07-28 core defines the extension mechanism and identifies Tasks as an opt-in extension, while the Tasks extension documentation still points to a draft specification and requires explicit support by both peers.

kjds_use_cases: Potential adapter for reporting state of long-running read-only tool jobs.
Potential interoperability mapping to existing KJDS agent-task and persisted-state contracts.
risks: The extension lifecycle, draft schema, and SDK implementations may change incompatibly.
Protocol task state can become a second canonical business state.
Cancellation semantics may not stop underlying side effects.
The 2025-11-25 and 2026-07-28 Tasks lifecycles are not wire-compatible and tasks/list was removed for unsafe scoping.

criteria: A versioned Tasks extension specification and the KJDS Python SDK path support the 2026-07-28 lifecycle without legacy fallback.
At least two required tool providers implement compatible task lifecycle behavior.
An adapter can preserve KJDS as the canonical task and business-state owner.
Conformance, cancellation, retry, expiry, and result-integrity tests pass.
Version drift and provider disagreement fail closed.
No external write or business-state transition is inferred from protocol status alone.

watch.decision_rationale: A2A 1.0 is released for cross-agent interoperability, but KJDS has no demonstrated need to expose agent cards or delegate governed business work across organizations.

maturity.evidence_basis: The A2A project announces version 1.0 as production-ready, but KJDS has not validated provider interoperability, trust, or authority mapping.

kjds_use_cases: Potential bounded delegation between a KJDS research agent and an independently operated partner agent.
Potential portable task status and artifact exchange without exposing internal orchestration.
risks: Remote agent identity, capability claims, and artifacts may be untrusted.
Delegation can obscure authority, Evidence lineage, cost, and accountability.
Protocol adoption may add no value over first-party APIs and MCP tools.

criteria: A real partner workflow requires cross-organization agent interoperability.
Agent identity, exact scope, artifact integrity, and cost ownership are specified.
Two independent implementations pass a read-only interoperability rehearsal.
Authentication, authorization, replay, cancellation, artifact, and failure tests pass.
Every remote conclusion remains an observation until KJDS Evidence review.
Delegation cannot grant Fact, FinanceEntry, Pilot, Permit, or external-write authority.

watch.decision_rationale: Bidirectional browser automation may reduce protocol-specific coupling, but WebDriver BiDi remains a W3C Working Draft and official Seller APIs remain the preferred integration path.

maturity.evidence_basis: WebDriver BiDi is published as a W3C Working Draft, not a Recommendation.

kjds_use_cases: Potential provider-neutral transport for isolated, deterministic, read-only browser capture.
Compare browser event and network observability with the existing Playwright harness.
risks: Draft protocol and browser implementations can drift.
Authenticated browser automation can leak cookies, profiles, personal data, or write capability.
UI automation is brittle and must not replace available official APIs.

criteria: Required browser implementations pass the same conformance subset.
A measured Playwright transport limitation blocks a required read-only workflow.
Disposable profile, no-cookie-persistence, and network allowlist controls are defined.
Ten of ten deterministic read-only replay fixtures pass across supported browsers.
Zero credential persistence, unexpected navigation, CAPTCHA bypass, or external write occurs.
The provider remains behind the KJDS browser adapter and human-takeover boundary.

watch.decision_rationale: Quantized local inference could lower extraction cost or improve data residency, but KJDS has no validated local-model quality, hardware, or unit-economics case and torchao includes mixed stable and prototype APIs.

maturity.evidence_basis: Official torchao documentation distinguishes stable workflows from prototype and experimental quantization paths.

kjds_use_cases: Potential low-cost OCR, classification, embedding, or redaction inference on controlled hardware.
Potential privacy-preserving fallback for non-decision workloads.
risks: Quantization can reduce multilingual extraction and calibration quality.
Prototype kernels and hardware-specific paths can regress or become unsupported.
GPU operations and model maintenance can cost more than managed inference.

criteria: A provider-neutral eval corpus identifies a non-decision workload with acceptable local-model quality.
Volume and data-residency requirements justify owned inference.
A stable hardware and software support matrix exists.
Quality, calibration, latency, throughput, energy, and total-cost thresholds beat the managed baseline.
Fallback, model provenance, vulnerability, and drift controls pass.
Local output remains an observation and cannot silently enter decision truth.

reject_now.decision_rationale: ClickHouse and Iceberg are capable technologies, but current KJDS volume and team topology do not justify separate real-time analytics and lakehouse truth planes beside PostgreSQL and Evidence storage.

maturity.evidence_basis: Official documentation describes ClickHouse real-time analytics and Iceberg v3 table features; rejection is based on KJDS fit, not an upstream maturity claim.

kjds_use_cases: Possible future high-volume event analytics with ClickHouse.
Possible future immutable analytical history and row lineage with Iceberg.
risks: Additional stores create synchronization, lineage, access-control, backup, and on-call burden.
A second analytics truth plane can diverge from PostgreSQL, Evidence, and financial ledgers.
Premature platform work delays profit truth and commercial validation.

criteria: Measured PostgreSQL workload misses an approved latency or retention SLO after indexing, partitioning, and query remediation.
Data volume, concurrency, or retention economics justify a second store with an assigned operator.
Canonical ownership, replication, reconciliation, deletion, residency, and recovery contracts are approved.
A disposable benchmark proves material cost or latency benefit on KJDS-shaped data.
Cross-store lineage, exact-scope isolation, replay, reconciliation, backup, and disaster recovery pass.
The analytical stores cannot become business Fact, FinanceEntry, or external-write owners.
